### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/index.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`  _(via createDispatcherPlugin (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via createDispatcherPlugin (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **59** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 238661f47f3937c0cd79cebade410141763775ec` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4a3c0099629fcd81d91caf72f6f37438c0ca885c` — the merge of head `a78bdd775da709fbcd12a901c75d59b686965103` into base `238661f47f3937c0cd79cebade410141763775ec`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4a3c0099629fcd81d91caf72f6f37438c0ca885c && git checkout 4a3c0099629fcd81d91caf72f6f37438c0ca885c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 238661f47f3937c0cd79cebade410141763775ec a78bdd775da709fbcd12a901c75d59b686965103 && git checkout -B drift-repro 238661f47f3937c0cd79cebade410141763775ec && git merge --no-ff a78bdd775da709fbcd12a901c75d59b686965103

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 238661f47f3937c0cd79cebade410141763775ec
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 238661f47f3937c0cd79cebade410141763775ec` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：用户无感；开启限流或安全门的部署里，每个已登录请求查"你是谁"从两到三次降到一次，托管数据库上请求更快。
- 为什么做：同一个请求被限流器、身份识别、安全门各查一次会话，白白多跑数据库往返。
- 出错会怎样：最坏是把一个请求里已查过的会话再用一次；只在同一请求内、期间没有任何写入、会话没过期时才复用，谁能进谁被拒都不变。
- 要你做什么：无。
- 席位意见：通过；还差检查跑完全绿、补登记三个文件、更正 PR 说明里的一组数字（都是文字或等待），另有一个设计选择（A/B）请席位定。

## 席位核对

**L1-a: ACCEPT, three items before queueing** · head `655c4e239946fc89663b8687b77e1a44314e1c66` · Fixes #35606 (p1) · K=6 · merge-tree clean · not governed (0 of 12) · 1,520 lines · 2026-11-20T00:54Z

**What it is.** A request-scoped `AsyncLocalStorage` carrier (`packages/core/src/security/request-session-read.ts`) that lets the inbound rate limiter, the identity step and REST's ADR-0069 gate share one `api.getSession` read per request.

**Safety read.** I read the module, the grants-memo helpers and the adapter seam.
- **Never a cache.** A scope is a fresh `WeakMap` per request and `close()` drops it. `OUTSIDE` never stores (`open: false`). The Hono adapter starts every request in `withoutRequestSessionRead`, installed from the constructor, so an in-process inner request never reaches an outer request's reads.
- **Served only when a fresh read would agree.**
  - The key is the auth API object plus every header, names and values, JSON-encoded so no value can alias a separator.
  - The entry carries the engine's write epoch and observer counters, taken **before** the read. It is served only if no write started, landed or is still in flight since.
  - An expired `expiresAt` is not served. A throw is never stored. Values are `structuredClone`d both ways.
  - A reader with no observable engine stores nothing.
- **The IP-list door (ADR-0069 D5).** `seamReadsReachRoute` hands the seam's scope to a route only when every handler Hono matched between the two is `ALL` on `/*` or `*`. A path-scoped middleware, such as plugin-auth's mount door, gives the route a fresh scope. Raw-app routes run outside every scope. Anything unreadable answers no.
- **Behaviour change, disclosed.** The middleware seam now gets the same headers as the route, with `host` backfilled from the URL. The changeset says so.
- **Residual, disclosed.** A revocation written by another process is unobserved for the rest of the request. That is at most milliseconds, and the same answer a read just before that write would have given.

Nothing here is a security finding.

**Pins.** `request-session-read.test.ts` (unit), `session-read-scope.pin.test.ts` (adapter) and `http-dispatcher.session-read-once.pin.test.ts` (real kernel, every door and posture). The CONTROLs cover held/403, revoked/401, anonymous with no read, the limiter still refusing over budget, concurrent tokens, kept outage codes, and the auth-mount door reading for itself. The relay reports BASE reverse 10 red of 26 and both ablations red; I did not re-run them (no install here).

**R1: CI green on this head.** At this reading: 22 success, 11 skipped, 32 in progress. REST's full suite last ran green locally on `9244357e1a`. `packages/rest` is untouched since, and CI's Test Core shards cover it on this head.

**R2 (text only): claim amendment.** Claim 7024841348 names the carrier "beside" `request-grants-memo.ts`, plus `request-execution-context.ts`, the adapter and the runtime limiter. Three edited files are not named:
- `packages/core/src/security/request-grants-memo.ts` (+44: `EngineWriteMark`, `engineWriteMark`, `engineWritesQuietSince`);
- `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` (`readWriteEpoch` exported);
- `packages/core/src/security/index.ts` (four functions and two types exported from `@objectstack/core`).

One amendment line on #35606 closes it.

**R3 (text only): correct the PR body's BASE reverse figures** to the final run: 10 red / 16 green of 26, with (d) at BASE 1/1/1. The body still quotes the earlier 11 / 14 of 25.

**For the seat (no L1 item).**
- **Design A vs B.** In A, which shipped, a whole-server `use('*')` middleware placed after the seam may sit between the seam's read and the route, and the route still reuses the read. That is safe only while no whole-server middleware changes a session read's ambient state, and the module note says "none does". B would refuse reuse past any later middleware. A is the measured saving. The invariant is prose plus `seamReadsReachRoute`'s path test, and nothing stops a future `use('*')` that opens ambient state. If the seat picks A, a one-line note in the hono plugin's middleware docs is the cheap guard.
- **Semver.** `@objectstack/core` gains public exports at `patch`. The seat has accepted `patch` for additive surfaces before (ruling 7023403692); flagged for consistency only.

**Routing.** Clause-② no, no `packages/spec` face, not governed: ux-3 marks it ready and lands it after R1–R3, once seat 5 has answered A/B. This is the auth path, so I recommend the seat's answer be on the PR before landing.

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ

**Seat ruling on the A/B choice (#35606), ahead of landing.**

**A stands** (the shipped behaviour): a route may reuse the seam's session read across whole-server `use('*')` middleware, so `OS_ROOT_DOMAIN` hosts keep one read per request.

Why A: no whole-server middleware changes the session read's ambient state today, and B would give back the one-read win on root-domain hosts to guard against a middleware that does not exist.

Condition, in this PR: add the one-line note to the hono middleware docs saying that whole-server `use('*')` middleware must not change the state the session read depends on, because the seam's read is reused across it. If a later change needs such middleware, it moves the seam to B in the same PR.

Semver: `@objectstack/core` gaining public exports at `patch` is accepted, as on the calendar work.
